record.original_question: Does there exist a pseudoconvex domain in C^2 with the same homotopy type as S 2 ?

evidence.quote: Problem 7.1.1 Does there exist a pseudoconvex domain in C2 with the same homotopy type as S 2 ? -F. Forstneric, forstner@math.wisc.edu 7.2 The Bergman Metric B

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ is called pseudoconvex if it admits a $\mathcal{C}^2$ plurisubharmonic exhaustion function, or equivalently if $-\log \operatorname{dist}(\,\cdot\,, \partial \Omega)$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$. Two topological spaces are said to have the same homotopy type if there exist continuous maps between them whose compositions are homotopic to the respective identity maps. Let $S^2$ denote the standard $2$-sphere.

Question: Does there exist a pseudoconvex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ that has the same homotopy type as $S^2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether there exists a Stein (or pseudoconvex) domain in $\mathbb{C}^2$ homotopy equivalent to $S^2$ is referenced as an open problem in subsequent literature (e.g., Forstnerič's 2003 J. Geom. Anal. paper "Stein domains in complex surfaces"). It is known that any embedded $2$-sphere in such a domain must be null-homologous, but the existence question itself appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Stein domains in complex surfaces (Forstnerič)
status_evidence.snippet: Asks whether there exists a Stein domain in C^2 homotopically equivalent to S^2; remarks the question is apparently still open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as still open in later work.

status_evidence.title: Stein Domains in Complex Surfaces (arXiv:math/0201097)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies which topological types occur as Stein domains in complex surfaces, discussing the S^2 case.
status_evidence.claim: Related study of admissible homotopy types of Stein domains in complex surfaces.
